analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by trusting the send callback return value when it equals the requested length but the pointer/length pair is stale for DTLS buffered data. In this PoV, outputBuffer.length is 164 while outputBuffer.buffer points to an allocation of only 274 bytes total with idx at end (0x...8d2), so fuzzer_send/memory_test/fwrite reads past allocation. SendBuffered only checks `sent > outputBuffer.length` and then advances idx/length, but does not validate that `outputBuffer.idx + outputBuffer.length` is within the actual allocated output buffer size before calling CBIOSend. The bad state is produced earlier by DTLS message pool/output buffer growth/flush interactions (DtlsMsgPoolSend/CheckAvailableSize/GrowOutputBuffer), and then consumed in SendBuffered.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Using DTLS client fuzz harness with randomized I/O, crafted handshake bytes drive ProcessReplyEx into DTLS handshake/message-pool paths, then fatal alert sending calls SendAlert_ex -> SendBuffered. The output buffer metadata becomes inconsistent (idx at buffer end while length remains non-zero), and SendBuffered passes `(buffer + idx, length)` to the send callback. The harness send callback performs a raw read of `sz` bytes (memory_test->fwrite), triggering deterministic heap-buffer-overflow read.
